name: Sauvage / Bleu de Chanel compliment getters
lead: "Compliment getter" is fragrance-community slang for a scent said to draw positive comments from other people. Dior Sauvage and Bleu de Chanel are two best-selling men's fragrances frequently named in this context.

Bleu de Chanel was released by the French house Chanel in 2010 as a woody aromatic fragrance created by perfumer Jacques Polge.[1] It won the 2011 FiFi Award for Best New Male Fragrance, and ranked among the best-selling men's fragrances in the US in 2011 and 2012.[1] No published study located for this article has tested whether either fragrance elicits more compliments or improves perceived attractiveness.
infobox: 2011 FiFi Award, Best New Male Fragrance

paras: Top notes include lemon, mint, pink pepper and grapefruit; heart notes include ginger, nutmeg, jasmine and Iso E Super; base notes include labdanum, sandalwood, patchouli, vetiver, incense, cedar and white musk.[1] Martin Scorsese directed the launch commercial, with actor Gaspard Ulliel as the first face of the fragrance from 2010 until his death in 2022.[1] Timothée Chalamet became ambassador in 2023.[1]
It was a top Christmas seller at Bloomingdale's in 2010 and the second most popular fragrance in Britain in 2021.[1]

Sources reviewed for this article did not provide verifiable details on the Dior Sauvage line; the Wikipedia article reviewed describes the earlier 1966 Dior men's fragrance Eau Sauvage by Edmond Roudnitska, which is a distinct product.

Fragrance communities discuss popular designer scents as "safe" or crowd-pleasing options and trade reports of compliments. These accounts are anecdotal; specific community sources were not available for citation.
No studies found. Broader research on fragrance and perceived attractiveness was not reviewed for this article.

card.summary: Two hugely popular men's designer scents that fragrance communities call crowd-pleasers; the compliment claims are anecdotal.
card.note: No studies test compliment rates; Sauvage coverage in sources is limited.

quick.overview:
Sauvage and Bleu de Chanel are among the best-selling men's fragrances and are often called "compliment getters" in fragrance communities.

Sales and awards are documented for Bleu de Chanel; claims about compliments are personal reports and have not been studied.
quick.mechanism: People wear a popular, widely liked scent and report on reactions from others.
quick.risks: Fragrance can cause skin allergy or breathing irritation in some people; otherwise main cost is price.
